title: Separate Unity metadata line endings from GUID validation
task_type: Unity Editor asset and build verification
environment: Line-oriented Unity metadata readers. The observed tool required lowercase hexadecimal GUIDs; this lesson does not establish that every Unity producer must use that casing or that arbitrary whitespace should be accepted.
goal: Validate Unity asset metadata before constructing an isolated verification project.
approach: Historical failed assumption: A multiline regular expression required the GUID capture to be followed immediately by the line-end anchor, without accounting for the carriage return preceding LF.
what_worked: Historical correction: Accept one optional carriage return outside the GUID capture. Retain the exact identifier syntax required by the tool, the exactly-one-GUID-line rule, duplicate-GUID checks, and the original asset/meta byte hashes. Do not normalize the entire metadata file merely to make an identity check pass. Verification reported by the source: Committed regressions cover successful preparation with LF and CRLF metadata and rejection of a malformed 31-character GUID with CRLF. The checkpoint records a 314/314 non-Unity harness pass; Unity was not launched for that checkpoint.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: Valid metadata using CRLF line endings was rejected as an invalid GUID before Unity launched. The same parser accepted LF metadata.
why: Confirmed by source inspection and the recorded input audit: CRLF left a carriage return outside the expected 32-character hexadecimal identifier, so a valid line failed the expression. This was a line-terminator incompatibility, not evidence of a corrupt identifier.
improved_method: Treat line terminators separately from identifier content. Test LF, CRLF, malformed identifiers, and duplicate identity declarations without weakening content or hash validation.
when_to_use: Line-oriented Unity metadata readers. The observed tool required lowercase hexadecimal GUIDs; this lesson does not establish that every Unity producer must use that casing or that arbitrary whitespace should be accepted.
when_not_to_use: The observed tool required lowercase hexadecimal GUIDs; this lesson does not establish that every Unity producer must use that casing or that arbitrary whitespace should be accepted.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
